articleTitle: Older oil filled electrical switchgear: past, present and future
publicationTitle: Symposium on Can I Afford to Lose My Main Switchboard? - The Management of Aged Oil-filled Switchgear in Industrial and Commercial Environments(DIgest No: 1997/079), IEE Colloquium on
abstract: Oil filled electrical switchgear has been in use both at high and low voltage for many years and has, of necessity, been of robust construction. This fact has led many to assume that it has an indefinite service life. There have been cases of high voltage switchgear installed 70 to 80 years ago still being in service. It is not uncommon to find both high and low voltage switchgear from the 1920's and 1930's still in use. Performance requirements for switchgear have risen over the years and switchgear technology has developed to meet the challenges. System fault energy levels have tended to increase as distribution networks have expanded to meet the ever increasing demands for energy. This has partially lead to the required improvements for the performance aspects of switchgear. Other improvements have arisen from operational needs. The author looks at some of the problem areas, the present position, and the future.

publicationTitle: Symposium on Can I Afford to Lose My Main Switchboard? - The Management of Aged Oil-filled Switchgear in Industrial and Commercial Environments(DIgest No: 1997/079), IEE Colloquium on
abstract: The UK Health and Safety Executive's (HSEs) concern relates to switchgear, such as oil circuit-breakers, oil-switches, oil-isolators etc., which is dependent manually operated or overstressed or both. They are interested in both high voltage and low voltage switchgear, though their efforts have been concentrated on the high voltage switchgear because of the greater risk. Some of the switchgear is very old and has not been properly maintained, there has been a decline in knowledge and expertise among the users, and some operators are not aware of the risks when closing onto circuits which could be faulty. Guidance was prepared to bring the problem to the attention of users. This takes the form of a free Information Document, giving information about the equipment concerned, the risks and the precautions that can be taken.

articleTitle: Times change-the safe certified solution [LV switchgear maintenance]
publicationTitle: Symposium on Can I Afford to Lose My Main Switchboard? - The Management of Aged Oil-filled Switchgear in Industrial and Commercial Environments(DIgest No: 1997/079), IEE Colloquium on
abstract: The author describes the results of a study into LV switchgear maintenance in which it soon became obvious that in order to provide equipment in accordance with the Health & Safety at Work Act and to comply with the current British Standard for Low Voltage Switchboards (BSEN 60439-1:1994), the only solution was to provide a complete replacement ACE cubicle. To meet these requirements, a comprehensive range of cubicles with various ratings and widths were designed and ASTA Certified to BSEN 60439-1:1994.

publicationTitle: Symposium on Can I Afford to Lose My Main Switchboard? - The Management of Aged Oil-filled Switchgear in Industrial and Commercial Environments(DIgest No: 1997/079), IEE Colloquium on
abstract: There are economic advantages of rejuvenating an existing switchboard, apart from the essentials of health and safety. It has been proven that by careful study of existing equipment (i.e. cubicles, bus bars, bus risers, cable boxes and cables), by retrofitting a new circuit breaker, existing short circuit ratings or enhanced ratings can be achieved. An ideal type of circuit breaker would be a vacuum breaker, for apart from their compact size they discharge no effluent and require a minimum of maintenance. Such switchgear maintenance is examined by the author in this paper.

articleTitle: The assessment and management of aged oil-filled switchgear
publicationTitle: Symposium on Can I Afford to Lose My Main Switchboard? - The Management of Aged Oil-filled Switchgear in Industrial and Commercial Environments(DIgest No: 1997/079), IEE Colloquium on
abstract: When considering the future of aged (pre-1960) oil-filled switchgear, a number of factors need to be considered. This paper examines these factors together with the modes/consequences of failure and the methods/techniques of failure prevention. The alternative options for dealing with aged industrial switchgear are explored with particular emphasis on the condition assessment approach. The available diagnostic techniques are described and their advantages/limitations identified. Also covered are the importance of including condition monitoring techniques in an effective maintenance strategy and the importance of high voltage insulation assessment in determining whether to replace or refurbish inadequate switchgear. The paper is essentially aimed at industrial/commercial organisations with oil circuit breaker (OCB) switchgear operating at 11 kV and 33 kV but the content is equally applicable to OCBs operating at other voltages such as 3.3 kV, 6.6 kV and 25 kV. In addition, many of the points discussed will apply to other oil-filled switchgear such as 11 kV oil switches, 11 kV oil switch fuses (or fuse switches) and low voltage oil switchgear.

articleTitle: Oil filled switchgear replacement-type testing and system issues
publicationTitle: Symposium on Can I Afford to Lose My Main Switchboard? - The Management of Aged Oil-filled Switchgear in Industrial and Commercial Environments(DIgest No: 1997/079), IEE Colloquium on
abstract: There is a growing interest in the economic replacement of ageing oil filled switchgear. Whether whole switchboards are renewed or partial replacement (sometimes referred to as retrofitting) is implemented the same obligation exists to achieve appropriate performance levels. Here, the author describes how the successful replacement of oil-filled switchgear requires an overall maintenance strategy, taking into account not only equipment but a review of the system as a whole.

articleTitle: An industrial user's view [of switchgear maintenance]
publicationTitle: Symposium on Can I Afford to Lose My Main Switchboard? - The Management of Aged Oil-filled Switchgear in Industrial and Commercial Environments(DIgest No: 1997/079), IEE Colloquium on
abstract: This paper describes the steps taken to assess the size of the problem of aged oil-filled switchgear, identify the options available, formulate policies and introduce action plans within a large industrial organisation. The methods used to monitor progress across a large number of sites are also discussed, together with some of the problems encountered.

articleTitle: Retrofit-a realistic option for switchgear replacement
publicationTitle: Symposium on Can I Afford to Lose My Main Switchboard? - The Management of Aged Oil-filled Switchgear in Industrial and Commercial Environments(DIgest No: 1997/079), IEE Colloquium on
abstract: The author describes how retrofitting can be a cost-effective way of replacing LV and HV distribution switchgear, keeping outage work and power system disruptions to a minimum, whilst upgrading the switchgear, control, protection and drawings. With the anticipated minimum of 25 years plant life extension, the large capital funding that would be required to replace whole switchboards can be avoided by the use of retrofitting in asset replacement programmes.
